summary: Anthropic describes the June 12 US export-control action that forced suspension of its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models over a reported cybersecurity jailbreak, the subsequent safety-classifier fix, the lifting of controls on June 30 and restoration of access, and new industry/government collaboration commitments on jailbreak severity scoring.

mechanisms.reason: The US government applied export controls restricting model access to foreign nationals and later lifted them, directly affecting which parties could access the models.
mechanisms.quote: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.

mechanisms.reason: Access to the suspended models is restored to users globally across multiple surfaces, reversing an earlier volume-suppressing suspension.
mechanisms.quote: Access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 is now restored.

practices.reason: The proposed four-criteria jailbreak severity framework gives teams a transferable method to score and triage jailbreak findings, though it is still being finalized with industry partners.
practices.quote: Our current proposal is to score a given jailbreak on the four different criteria below.

practices.reason: Usage limits, credit-based access after a fixed date, and phased re-enablement across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry create concrete scheduling and quota work for teams integrating Fable 5.
practices.quote: Fable 5 will be included for up to 50% of weekly usage limits through July 7, after which it will be available via usage credits .

notable_reason: A first-of-its-kind government export-control action forcing suspension of a frontier model over a cybersecurity jailbreak, followed by resolution and new government-industry safety collaboration commitments, is a significant regulatory precedent for the sector.
